goal.title: Implement csm-orchestrate as an active cross-skill CSM outer loop
goal.outcome: Coordinate all repository skills to deliver end-to-end outcomes through approach-phase compilation, thin-slice execution, typed evidence, adversarial review, final review, bounded remediation, and long-horizon recovery.
constraints: Preserve sibling skill domain logic, artifacts, ownership, internal lifecycles, and side-effect authority.
Use canonical JSON artifacts and registered schemas; Markdown is never authoritative machine input.
Require explicit approval before mutation, commits, credentials, browser actions, publication, destructive work, or promotion.
Final review is mandatory and may create a new bounded remediation phase.
All implementation tasks remain pending until a separate explicit csm-build invocation.
exclusions: Do not duplicate sibling skill logic.
Do not create an unrestricted autonomous agent loop.
Do not silently invoke every skill or flatten child states.
Do not claim productivity or correctness improvement without evaluation evidence.

design.boundary: csm-orchestrate owns parent outcome, requirement ledger, route graph, child invocation, evidence reconciliation, approvals, checkpoints, adversarial acceptance, final review, and receipt; sibling skills own domain work and artifacts.
design.thinSlice: approach phase -> phase contract -> selected route -> one bounded increment -> typed receipt -> requirement/evidence mapping -> technical gate -> functional gate -> adversarial review -> final review -> checkpoint
design.phaseInsertion: Final review creates a new phase only with unique phaseId, parentPhaseId, graph revision, insertedAfter, requirementDelta, owner/route, acceptance signals, approval scope, idempotency policy, and remediation budget. Cycle, duplicate, stale, and already-executed side-effect checks fail closed.
design.statusSeparation: Keep route state, child lifecycle, artifact lifecycle, verification result, approval state, and parent outcome as separate fields.
design.authoritativeInputs: Registered canonical JSON approach artifacts are authoritative; Markdown requires an explicit projection adapter with source identity/digest validation.

verificationStrategy.perTask: Every task has one primary acceptance signal and supporting negative tests; all task statuses remain pending until csm-build executes them.
verificationStrategy.final: Require every critical requirement verified, no unresolved critical evidence, valid child lineage, passing technical and functional gates, adversarial acceptance, mandatory final review, and safe checkpoint/receipt publication.
verificationStrategy.environment: Host invocation and side-effect tests must use isolated synthetic fixtures; no live credentials or production services.

risks: Automatic dispatch could bypass sibling boundaries.
Conflicting native IDs/paths/statuses could corrupt lineage.
A final-review-created phase could form a cycle or repeat a side effect.
A child narrative could be mistaken for outcome evidence.
Retrying a non-idempotent action could duplicate external effects.
A model or reviewer could game an acceptance rubric.
Uncommitted concurrent work could be overwritten.
mitigations: Capability manifest and host enforcement fail closed.
Adapters normalize IDs and preserve source identity.
Immutable phase parentage, graph revision, cycle detection, and idempotency keys.
Fresh reviewer context, calibrated rubrics, hidden acceptance cases, and human review.
Build uses owned paths only and preserves unrelated worktree changes.
risksAndRecovery.rollback: Never rewrite producer artifacts. Revert or supersede only orchestrator-owned nonterminal state using new run/phase identity; external effects require route-specific compensation or human reconciliation.
